component.name: Nubo
component.summary: Play Game Boy and Game Boy Color games

description.p: Nubo is a cycle-accurate Game Boy and Game Boy Color emulator. It emulates every model from the first Game Boy to the Game Boy Advance and is checked against thousands of hardware test ROMs.

Nubo is made almost entirely by AI. Nearly all of its code and documentation, and even its name, were written by Claude, Anthropic's AI model, working in Claude Code. Its developer decides what Nubo should do, reviews the changes and chooses what goes in. It started as a fork of RetroBoy by Samuel Parsons. If you'd rather not use software made this way, that's a fair choice, and it's why this is said up front.

ul.li: A game library built from your ROM folders, with each game's title screen or box art
Save states with pictures, and continuing where you left off
Fast forward, fullscreen and screenshots
Keyboard and controller controls you can change, and menus you can use with a controller
GameShark and Game Genie cheats
Gray, green or Pocket colors for Game Boy games, and light and dark themes

description.p: Nubo comes without games: it plays the ROM files (.gb, .gbc or .zip) you add.
The screenshot shows Tobu Tobu Girl Deluxe by Tangram Games, licensed under CC BY 4.0.

screenshot.caption: Playing Tobu Tobu Girl Deluxe by Tangram Games

description.p: Nubo can start over from its settings, its menus wrap around, and the controller's triggers no longer load or save by accident.

ul.li: Start over, on the settings' About tab, puts the settings back to how they started and can also delete the in-game saves and save states, remove the game folders and clear Continue playing; it asks first, and a reset that deletes nothing can be undone
Up on the first row of a menu goes to the last, and down on the last goes to the first, in the pause menu, the library, the settings and the dialogs

The controller's L2 and R2 are no longer quick load and quick save at first, since they are easy to press by accident; both are still in the pause menu, and controls you already set keep their buttons
Nubo.app, built with cargo xtask macos, shows its icon in Finder and the Dock straight away, instead of a blank one
Save states made by Nubo 0.4.0 to 0.9.1 still load

description.p: Nubo's command line is easier to use: on Linux it explains itself, and everywhere it takes any file name.

ul.li: On Linux, --help lists the command line options and --version prints the version
Games whose path isn't valid UTF-8 now open from the command line
Save states made by Nubo 0.4.0 to 0.9.0 still load

description.p: Nubo is friendlier for players who just want to play: rewind, a library with real game names and menus, undo for loads and restarts, and an emulator that needs about a third less work for the same, exact result.

ul.li: Rewind: hold R, or the controller's left face button, to go back through the last 30 seconds
Game Boy Color games show softer colors, closer to its own screen (Color correction, on by default), and Smooth out flicker makes blinking sprites look see-through as on the real screen
Loading a state, restarting and saving over a slot can be undone from the message they show

Library games show their real names, have a menu (right click, the ⋯ button or Select) to play them on another model, show them in their folder or delete their save states, and can be sorted by name, last played or last added
Pick the model by console first, then its revision, each with a sentence saying what it is
Automatic starts Super Game Boy games on the Super Game Boy again, with their colors and border
The game pauses while another window is in front, the mouse pointer hides while you play, the window opens at its last size, and the game bar has a volume slider
Leaving a game goes back from fullscreen to a window, and the library has an Exit fullscreen button
The browser version offers to play your last game again, and the desktop app can tell you about new versions if you want
Box art is downloaded only after you say yes, and a narrow window shows the settings' tabs above the page
Nubo needs 20 to 40% fewer instructions per frame, with every frame, sound and save state exactly as before
The RetroArch core keeps saving states, rewinding and running ahead after a restart onto a Super Game Boy
Save states made by Nubo 0.4.0 to 0.8.1 still load

description.p: Nubo now brings its own fonts, so it looks the same on Windows, macOS, Linux and in the browser.

ul.li: Text is drawn in DejaVu Sans and titles in Liberation Sans Bold everywhere, instead of whatever font the system has
Titles in the browser are bold now too
Save states made by Nubo 0.4.0 to 0.8.0 still load

description.p: Nubo is simpler to use: the game screen's bar keeps only what you reach for while playing, the pause menu opens with a right click, the settings are tidied into clear pages, and games continue where you left off.

ul.li: The game screen's bar now has a Library button, the game's name, fast forward, sound, fullscreen and a Pause button. Restart game, Screenshot and Settings are in the pause menu
A right click on the game opens the pause menu, as Esc does, and a click on the game outside the menu closes it and resumes the game
Double-click the game to switch fullscreen on and off. In fullscreen the bar is at the top of the screen again
The settings have five pages: Display, Playing, Controls, Library and About, each laid out the same way. No setting was added or removed, and your settings are kept
The library's bar has a named Open ROM button; Rescan is in the settings' Library page
Games can be taken off Continue playing with the X on their card, and games whose files are deleted leave the list at once
Continue games where you left off is now on for new installs
Automatic now starts Super Game Boy games on a plain Game Boy, or a Game Boy Color for color games. Pick the Super Game Boy in the settings for its colors and borders
Cartridges with RAM but no memory controller, which test programs use, now run
Save states made by Nubo 0.4.0 to 0.7.0 still load

description.p: Super Game Boy games can now be played by up to four players and get the Super Game Boy's colors, borders and intro, and Nubo for Windows now installs from an MSI, Windows' own installer format.

ul.li: Super Game Boy games for several players can be played by up to four, each with their own controller, in the app and on RetroArch's ports 1 to 4

The pause menu has a Super Game Boy page to pick the colors (the game's, Gray, Green, Pocket or your own, with an editor) and the border (the game's, Nubo's or none), shown at once over the paused game. RetroArch has the same choices as core options. Your choices are kept in the settings, and loading a save state doesn't change them
Games can take the color choices away or take their own colors back, as on a real Super Game Boy
Games on the Super Game Boy start after a short intro, as on the real one, which holds the Game Boy back while its intro plays. Nubo plays a silent intro of its own
Left alone for seven minutes, Nubo's border plays a screensaver of drifting clouds, unless the game turns it off
The Windows installer is now an MSI (Nubo-windows-x64.msi). Windows itself uninstalls Nubo from Settings, and installing still needs no administrator rights
The installer asks whether to open Game Boy games with Nubo and whether to add a desktop shortcut, can start Nubo when it is done, and keeps your choices when it updates Nubo
Installing an older version over a newer one is possible, after a warning about settings and save states
Nubo can be installed from the command line without any questions with msiexec, with the choices as ASSOCIATE_FILES and DESKTOP_SHORTCUT
Nightly builds show as "Nubo (nightly date)" in the list of installed apps on Windows
A security fix in the connection that box art is downloaded over
If you installed Nubo 0.6.0 or earlier with the old Windows installer, uninstall it from Settings first; your saves and settings stay
Save states made by Nubo 0.4.0, 0.5.0 and 0.6.0 still load

description.p: Nubo now runs in RetroArch, the original Game Boy's grays are drawn as the hardware shows them, and test programs can run Nubo from the command line.

ul.li: A RetroArch core for Windows, Linux and macOS, with save states, rewind, run-ahead, netplay, cheats, RetroAchievements and rumble. It is experimental and installed by hand
The original Game Boy's four shades are now evenly spaced, as on the hardware, so dark gray is no longer too light. The Gray palette shows them as they are; the other palettes still recolor them

New command-line options for test programs such as the GB Emulator Shootout: --scale shows only the game screen at a whole multiple of its size, --fresh starts like a new install and leaves nothing behind, and --speed starts fast forwarding
A mistake on the command line, including an unknown --model, now stops Nubo with a message instead of being ignored
Save states save about 15 times and load about 10 times faster
A damaged save state that could upset the picture's timing is now refused
Save states made by Nubo 0.4.0 and 0.5.0 still load

description.p: Games on MBC3 cartridges, such as Pokémon Gold, Silver and Crystal, now switch banks and read their clock as real cartridges do, and two picture glitches are fixed.

ul.li: The Japanese Pokémon Crystal and other games with a large MBC3 cartridge (the MBC30) now run
The cartridge clock in MBC3 games reads back the way the real chip does: a time written to the clock shows after the next latch, and any write to the latch register latches it
Switching to a bank number the cartridge doesn't have now gives what the real cartridge gives, instead of the previous bank
The window, a layer games use for menus and status bars, no longer starts a line too far down when a game turns it on at the right edge of the screen
Changing where background tiles come from at the top of the screen in Game Boy Color double speed mode no longer draws a mixed-up tile
Save states made by Nubo 0.4.0 still load

description.p: Save states now keep working when Nubo is updated.

ul.li: Save states store every value with its name, so later versions of Nubo load them, and earlier versions load newer ones as far as they can
A save state made on Linux, macOS or Windows loads on the others
Every change to Nubo is now checked against save states that earlier versions made
A save state made with another version of a game, such as a patched copy, is refused instead of loaded into the wrong game

Save states made by Nubo 0.3.0 and earlier can't be loaded by this version, because the new format is what keeps later updates from breaking them. Nubo keeps such a state next to its slot instead of overwriting it. In-game saves are not affected

description.p: A small release that smooths the browser version on power-saving browsers and corrects a license text.

ul.li: Browsers that save power by drawing only 30 times a second, such as Chrome with Energy Saver on, now get two frames on every refresh, so the picture no longer stutters every few seconds
The third-party licenses that come with Nubo for Windows give the Boost Software License's exact text
An installer for Windows that needs no administrator rights, with a Start menu entry, an uninstaller and an option to open Game Boy games with Nubo
A zip for Windows to run Nubo without installing it
Nubo has its own icon on Windows and no longer opens a console window next to it
Downloads are named after their system, and the README links to the latest ones

description.p: The first release of Nubo: a cycle-accurate Game Boy and Game Boy Color emulator that passes thousands of hardware test ROMs.

ul.li: Every model from the first Game Boy to the Game Boy Advance
A game library with title screens and box art
Save states, fast forward, fullscreen and screenshots
Keyboard and controller controls you can change
GameShark and Game Genie cheats
